editor_note: None of the four rewritten entries (4, 12, 15, 19) changes the meaning, but three need small edits. In entry 19, the card title "Propagated noise absorption" became "Pagsipsip ng ipinalaganap na ingay", while every other addon card title stays in English. Entry 30 also keeps "propagated noise absorption (PNA)", and the page otherwise uses "noise", not "ingay". A learner therefore cannot connect this card to PNA. Entry 19 also turns "Mitigate" into "Pagaanin", even though entry 26 uses "I-mitigate", and entry 15 adds an awkward gloss, "pag-learn (pagtukoy)". Entries 4 and 12 are faithful.

examples.source: title="Propagated noise absorption"
examples.translation: title="Pagsipsip ng ipinalaganap na ingay"
examples.suggested: title="Propagated noise absorption"
examples.why: This is the addon's name. Every other card title is kept in English, and entry 30 refers to it as "propagated noise absorption (PNA)". Translating the title, and using "ingay" when the page otherwise says "noise", makes it hard to tell that both refer to the same tool.

examples.source: Mitigate expectation values by measuring a target observable that has absorbed noise model information.
examples.translation: Pagaanin ang mga expectation value sa pamamagitan ng pagsukat ng target na observable na sumipsip ng impormasyon ng noise model.
examples.suggested: I-mitigate ang mga expectation value sa pamamagitan ng pagsukat ng target na observable na sumipsip ng impormasyon ng noise model.
examples.why: "Pagaanin" (to lighten or ease) reads oddly with expectation values. Entry 26 uses "I-mitigate" for the same verb, so this makes the page inconsistent.

examples.line_approx: intro sentence under Learn noise models
examples.source: Use the following tools for learning and refining noise models
examples.translation: Gamitin ang mga sumusunod na tool para sa pag-learn (pagtukoy) at pagpino ng mga noise model
examples.suggested: Gamitin ang mga sumusunod na tool para sa pagtukoy at pagpino ng mga noise model
examples.why: The gloss in parentheses reads like a translator's note, not published prose. "Pagtukoy" on its own is enough.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout, including the one-hot/set-packing constraint handling, the penalty paths, the iterative warm-start chains and the benchmark notes, so nothing here would mislead a learner. A few small edits remain. In [23], "well above 100 binary variables" becomes just "higit sa 100", which drops the emphasis. "Convert" is spelled two ways ("ikokonberti" in [17], "kino-convert" in [18]). In [51], "ve-verify" is a malformed verb, and "handles" is calqued as "hinahawakan" several times ([7], [17], [56]), which reads stiffly.

examples.source: with well above 100 binary variables
examples.translation: na may higit sa 100 binary variable
examples.suggested: na may higit na higit sa 100 binary variable
examples.why: Dropping 'well' slightly weakens the benchmark claim; it still does not mislead.

examples.source: it will first be transformed to a one-hot constraint
examples.translation: ito muna ay ikokonberti sa one-hot constraint
examples.suggested: iko-convert muna ito sa one-hot constraint
examples.why: The spelling differs from 'kino-convert' in [18]; one form should be used throughout the file.

examples.source: Finally we retrieve the solution and verify for correctness.
examples.translation: Sa huli, kukunin natin ang solusyon at ve-verify ang katumpakan nito.
examples.suggested: Sa huli, kukunin natin ang solusyon at iva-verify kung tama ito.
examples.why: 've-verify' is not a well-formed Taglish verb; the future form needs the 'i-' prefix (iva-verify).

examples.source: The function handles reformulation, circuit synthesis, transpilation, and hardware execution automatically.
examples.translation: Awtomatikong hinahawakan ng function ang reformulation, ...
examples.suggested: Awtomatikong ginagawa/inaasikaso ng function ang reformulation, ...
examples.why: 'Hinahawakan' (literally 'holds/touches') is a calque of 'handles'; 'inaasikaso' or 'ginagawa' reads more natural.

editor_note: The rewritten entry 6 keeps the English meaning. It says Estimator runs workloads on IBM Quantum resources, that PUBs are the inputs to run(), and that the result format depends on both the PUBs and the runtime options, so nothing here would mislead a learner. There are two small style problems. The English "Then, after the job has completed" became "Pagkatapos, pagkatapos makumpleto ang job", which repeats "pagkatapos" back to back. And "tinukoy mula sa primitive" is a word-for-word copy of the English "from the primitive" that a native editor would smooth out. "istraktura ng data" here matches entry 20.

examples.source: Then, after the job has completed, the results are returned
examples.translation: Pagkatapos, pagkatapos makumpleto ang job, ang mga resulta ay ibinabalik
examples.suggested: Kapag nakumpleto na ang job, ibinabalik ang mga resulta
examples.why: The same word "pagkatapos" appears twice in a row because each English word was translated separately. A native technical writer would merge them into one clause.

examples.source: the runtime options specified from the primitive
examples.translation: mga runtime option na tinukoy mula sa primitive
examples.suggested: mga runtime option na itinakda sa primitive
examples.why: "mula sa" copies the English preposition "from" literally. "itinakda sa" (set on) sounds more natural for options configured on the primitive.

editor_note: None of the four rewritten entries would mislead a learner. Entry 15 keeps the exclusive-access claim, the calibration-job exclusion and the queuing benefit intact. Two small things are worth fixing. First, the headings in entries 4, 7 and 14 now read "Mode na Job/Batch/Session", but the body text of the same page says "job mode", "batch mode" and "session mode" (entries 5, 12, 17), so each mode has one name in its heading and another in the text below it. Second, entry 15 ends with "sa iyong lokal na makina" ("your local machine"), which changes the source's generic "a user's local machine" into direct address to the reader.

examples.source: Batch mode {#batch-mode}
examples.translation: Mode na Batch {#batch-mode}
examples.suggested: Batch mode {#batch-mode}
examples.why: The body text uses 'batch mode' (entry 12, 'Para tumakbo sa batch mode'). A heading of 'Mode na Batch' splits the name of the same mode. The same applies to 'Mode na Job' (entry 4) vs 'job mode' (entry 5) and 'Mode na Session' (entry 14) vs 'session mode' (entry 17).

examples.source: running on a user's local machine.
examples.translation: na tumatakbo sa iyong lokal na makina.
examples.suggested: na tumatakbo sa lokal na makina ng user.
examples.why: The source says 'a user's' machine, meaning any user. The translation says 'your' machine, addressing the reader. The rest of the paragraph talks about 'ang user' in the third person, so this switch is inconsistent. It does not mislead, but it is a small change of meaning.

editor_note: The translation is faithful overall. It keeps the difficult "respectively, by orders of magnitude" comparison in the HI-VQE row ("ayon sa pagkakasunod, nang ilang order of magnitude") and all of the ZNE/PEC outperformance claims. In the Singularity row, the qualifier "significantly fewer learners" loses "significantly" and becomes plain "mas kaunting learner", which weakens the claim a little. The Optimization Solver row translates "high-level problem definitions" as "kahulugan ng problema", which reads as "the meaning of the problem". Entry [8] also calques "Each is performant for..." as "Ang bawat isa ay performant para sa...".

examples.source: while operating with significantly fewer learners and a more compact ensemble
examples.translation: habang nag-ooperate na may mas kaunting learner at mas compact na ensemble
examples.suggested: habang gumagamit ng mas kakaunting learner nang malaki at mas compact na ensemble
examples.why: The qualifier 'significantly' is dropped, which weakens the size of the efficiency claim. This is a dropped qualifier and counts as MINOR, not misleading.

examples.source: enables inputs of high-level problem definitions
examples.translation: nagbibigay-daan sa mga input ng high-level na kahulugan ng problema
examples.suggested: nagbibigay-daan na mag-input ng high-level na depinisyon ng problema
examples.why: 'Kahulugan' means 'meaning' or 'sense', but here the English means a formal problem specification, so 'depinisyon' or 'pagtukoy' is more accurate.

examples.source: Each is performant for specific workload characteristics
examples.translation: Ang bawat isa ay performant para sa mga partikular na katangian ng workload
examples.suggested: Mahusay ang performance ng bawat isa para sa mga partikular na uri ng workload
examples.why: This copies the English sentence structure and leaves the English adjective 'performant' in place. A native technical writer would rephrase it.

editor_note: The rewritten heading in entry 2, "Workflow ng development", means the same as the English and would not mislead a learner. The problem is consistency. Entry 1, the same "Development workflow" label, keeps the English, and the body text in entry 3 uses "development workflow" ("ay naglalarawan ng development workflow"). So the page title or sidebar label and the section heading will show two different wordings for one concept. Pick one wording for entries 1, 2 and 3; the simplest fix is to match entry 1 and entry 3 by using "Development workflow" in entry 2.

examples.source: Development workflow {#development-workflow}
examples.translation: Workflow ng development {#development-workflow}
examples.suggested: Development workflow {#development-workflow}
examples.why: The meaning is right, but the wording differs from entry 1 ("Development workflow") and from the running text in entry 3 ("development workflow"). The same label then shows up two ways on one page.

editor_note: Rewritten heading [33] "Simulation ng Clifford" is faithful and natural Tagalog; it sits fine beside the body's retained "Clifford simulation" in [34], and the anchor {#clifford-simulation} is untouched.

Neither rewritten entry would mislead a learner. Entry 27 is faithful: "mas sopistikadong implementasyon", "bilang isang cloud-based na serbisyo" and "ginagamit para ma-access ang IBM Quantum hardware" all match the English, and it needs no change. Entry 34 has the right meaning, including the "might be able to" hedge (maaari) and the "rather than building your own" contrast. It has one grammar slip, though. "maaari kang mas madaling ma-access" pairs the patient-focus verb "ma-access" with the actor pronoun "kang", and a native editor would write "maaari mong mas madaling ma-access". Also, "bumuo ng sariling implementasyon" drops the "your" that "iyong" would supply.

examples.source: you might be able to more easily access advanced hardware capabilities of a given provider
examples.translation: maaari kang mas madaling ma-access ang mga advanced na kakayahan ng hardware
examples.suggested: maaari mong mas madaling ma-access ang mga advanced na kakayahan ng hardware
examples.why: The patient-focus verb ma-access takes the ng-form actor pronoun (mo), not the ang-form (ka). As written it is ungrammatical, though still understandable.

examples.source: rather than building your own implementation of these techniques
examples.translation: sa halip na bumuo ng sariling implementasyon ng mga pamamaraang ito
examples.suggested: sa halip na bumuo ng iyong sariling implementasyon ng mga pamamaraang ito
examples.why: Drops 'your'. Adding 'iyong' matches the second-person voice used in the rest of the paragraph.

editor_note: Entry 8 is faithful and natural ("binuo gamit ang mga sumusunod na requirement … o mas bago"). Entry 24 keeps the disclaimer's hedged meaning, but it has two slips. First, "ang mga classical sample … ay maaaring makamit ang magkatulad na … kalidad" puts the actor in the ang-slot of an object-focus verb (makamit), so it reads like calqued English syntax; an actor-focus form such as "maaaring umabot sa" or "maaaring makakuha ng" would fix it. Second, the final sentence drops "therefore", which loses the link between the caveat and the advice to evaluate the whole workflow. Neither slip would mislead a learner.

examples.source: classical samples and quantum-generated samples might achieve similar final solution quality after equivalent post-processing
examples.translation: ang mga classical sample at quantum-generated sample ay maaaring makamit ang magkatulad na huling kalidad ng solusyon matapos ang katumbas na post-processing
examples.suggested: maaaring umabot sa magkatulad na huling kalidad ng solusyon ang mga classical sample at ang mga quantum-generated sample matapos ang katumbas na post-processing
examples.why: Makamit is object-focus, but here the actor sits in the ang-slot. That is a calqued, ungrammatical structure. An actor-focus verb reads natively.

examples.source: Evaluation should therefore consider the complete optimization workflow.
examples.translation: Dapat isaalang-alang ng ebalwasyon ang kumpletong optimization workflow.
examples.suggested: Kaya dapat isaalang-alang sa ebalwasyon ang kumpletong optimization workflow.
examples.why: 'Therefore' is dropped, so the reader loses the reasoning that ties the caveat to the advice. This is a minor dropped connective, not a change in meaning.

editor_note: None of the three rewritten entries would mislead a learner. There are two small fixes. In entry 45, "dahil mayroon itong isang tamang sagot" blurs the key point of "a single correct answer": "isang" can be read as just "a", so the reason Bernstein–Vazirani works as a benchmark (exactly one right answer) is weakened. "iisang tamang sagot" keeps that emphasis. Also, headings 33 and 43 now use Tagalog linker order ("Primitive na Estimator", "Primitive na Sampler"), but the body text right below keeps the English order ("Estimator primitive ng Fire Opal…", "Sampler primitive ng Fire Opal…"). Both orders are fine on their own, but the page should pick one.

examples.source: is a common benchmarking algorithm because there is a single correct answer.
examples.translation: ay isang karaniwang benchmarking algorithm dahil mayroon itong isang tamang sagot.
examples.suggested: ay isang karaniwang benchmarking algorithm dahil iisa lamang ang tamang sagot nito.
examples.why: 'isang' can be read as the article 'a', which weakens the point that there is exactly one correct answer. That uniqueness is why the algorithm is useful for benchmarking.

examples.source: Sampler primitive {#sampler-primitive}
examples.translation: Primitive na Sampler {#sampler-primitive}
examples.suggested: Keep 'Primitive na Sampler' and change the body to 'primitive na Sampler ng Fire Opal…' (entries 35/45), or put the headings back to 'Sampler primitive'.
examples.why: The headings (33, 43) use Tagalog linker order, but the body text right below them (35, 45) keeps the English order 'Sampler/Estimator primitive'. Both orders work, but mixing them on one page is inconsistent.

editor_note: All six rewritten entries are accurate; entry 7 keeps the negation and concession ("hindi makikita ng mga user... kahit na may access sila"), and entry 21 keeps "minimum set of permissions" as "pinakamaliit na hanay ng mga permisong kailangan".

Entry 6 is faithful: it keeps the "typically" hedge ("karaniwang may implicit reset na idiniinsert sa simula ng circuit") and renders "set as a primitive execution option" correctly ("na itinakda bilang isang primitive execution option"), and the Taglish verbs idiniinsert and naininitialize are consistent with entry 10.

Both rewritten entries keep the meaning of the English: "Get program arguments" becomes "Kunin ang ... Argumento ng Programa" and "Distribute task across workers" becomes "Ipamahagi ang Gawain sa mga Worker". Nothing in them would mislead a learner. The only problem is capitalization. Both use English-style Title Case ("Kunin ang Mga Argumento ng Programa", "Ipamahagi ang Gawain"), but the source is in sentence case and Tagalog never capitalizes "Mga" or common nouns in the middle of a sentence. This looks machine-generated and doesn't match the sentence-case headings on the rest of the page, such as "I-update ang eksperimento".

examples.source: Get program arguments
examples.translation: Kunin ang Mga Argumento ng Programa
examples.suggested: Kunin ang mga argumento ng programa
examples.why: The English is in sentence case, but this adds Title Case, which is not used in Tagalog. A capitalized "Mga" in the middle of a sentence reads as machine output.

examples.source: Distribute task across workers
examples.translation: Ipamahagi ang Gawain sa mga Worker
examples.suggested: Ipamahagi ang gawain sa mga worker
examples.why: The Title Case is also inconsistent within this one line: "Gawain" and "Worker" are capitalized but "mga" is not. The meaning is faithful.

editor_note: Rewritten entry 46 keeps "Pasqal Cloud Services" as the product name and appends "(PCS)", an abbreviation the source never spells out even though entries 48 and 51 use "PCS"; the addition is accurate, harmless and helps the reader, and the anchor {#pasqal-cloud-services} is unchanged.

Rewritten entry 29 keeps every clause of the Credly notice: data shared ("pangalan, email address, at badge na nakuha"), the "Maaaring ibahagi ng IBM" hedge, "sa buong mundo", and both privacy-statement links, with a consistent inyo/kayo register and no po/opo.

Entry 23 "Organisasyong Enterprise" renders the "Enterprise organization" heading faithfully, and it matches how the sibling headings keep English loan terms ("Akademikong institusyon, research organization, o QIC"; "Mga global systems integrator").

None of the four rewritten entries would mislead a learner. Entry 16 drops the qualifier "usually" from "its specifications usually include the number of cores", so the Tagalog states it as always true. It also writes "unit ng pagsukat" where entry 70 of the same delta uses "yunit ng impormasyon". In entry 70, "maaari lamang umabot sa estado 0 o 1" uses "umabot" ("reach") for "adopt", and the relative clause with a stray comma before "ay maaaring" copies the English sentence structure. Entries 7 ("Modelo ng Resource") and 108 ("Pagtatantya ng laki ng database...") are faithful.

examples.source: When purchasing a laptop, its specifications usually include the number of cores.
examples.translation: Kapag bumibili ng laptop, kasama sa mga espesipikasyon nito ang bilang ng mga core.
examples.suggested: Kapag bumibili ng laptop, karaniwang kasama sa mga espesipikasyon nito ang bilang ng mga core.
examples.why: The hedge 'usually' was dropped, which makes the claim slightly stronger. This is a minor dropped qualifier, not misleading.

examples.source: units of information which unlike their classical counterparts (which can only adopt the state 0 or 1), can be in a superposition of 0 and 1 simultaneously.
examples.translation: mga yunit ng impormasyon na hindi tulad ng kanilang mga klasikal na katapat (na maaari lamang umabot sa estado 0 o 1), ay maaaring nasa superposition ng 0 at 1 nang sabay-sabay.
examples.suggested: mga yunit ng impormasyon na, hindi tulad ng mga klasikal na bit (na maaari lamang nasa estado 0 o 1), ay maaaring nasa superposition ng 0 at 1 nang sabay-sabay.
examples.why: 'umabot' ('reach') is the wrong verb for 'adopt a state', and the comma placement copies the English clause structure.

examples.source: performance-related units of measurement
examples.translation: mga unit ng pagsukat
examples.suggested: mga yunit ng pagsukat
examples.why: The same word is written 'unit' here but 'yunit' in entry 70 (and entry 23). The two spellings should be made consistent.

editor_note: Entry 16 keeps the whole Credly notice intact, including the hedges ("Maaaring ibahagi ng IBM ... sa buong mundo" for "may share ... globally") and the data list (pangalan, email address, at badge na natamo), and it reads naturally.

Entry 11, the rewritten Credly privacy notice, keeps the English meaning. The data processor is authorized by IBM and located in the United States, the three data items (pangalan, email address, badge na nakuha) are all there, the purposes are the same, "Maaaring ibahagi" keeps "may share" as a possibility, and sharing still covers subsidiaries and third parties "sa buong mundo". Nothing is inverted, dropped or added. The only thing an editor would change is formatting: in both links the sentence's final period was moved inside the link text ("[dito.](...)"). It should sit outside the link, as in the English "[here](...).".

examples.source: The IBM Privacy Statement can be viewed [here](https://www.ibm.com/privacy/us/). IBM employees can view the IBM Internal Privacy Statement [here](https://w3.ibm.com/w3publisher/w3-privacy-notice).
examples.translation: Maaaring tingnan ang IBM Privacy Statement [dito.](https://www.ibm.com/privacy/us/) Matitingnan ng mga empleyado ng IBM ang IBM Internal Privacy Statement [dito.](https://w3.ibm.com/w3publisher/w3-privacy-notice)
examples.suggested: Maaaring tingnan ang IBM Privacy Statement [dito](https://www.ibm.com/privacy/us/). Matitingnan ng mga empleyado ng IBM ang IBM Internal Privacy Statement [dito](https://w3.ibm.com/w3publisher/w3-privacy-notice).
examples.why: The sentence's period was moved inside the link text, so the rendered link is underlined as 'dito.' The meaning is unchanged, but it doesn't match the source and a native editor would put the period back outside the link.

editor_note: The three rewritten entries are faithful. Entry 4 renders "simulating hadrons and spin glasses" as "pagsi-simulate ng mga hadron at spin glass", entry 43 keeps the "bago pa natin hayaan itong mag-evolve" ordering and "exponentiated na Hamiltonian", and entry 53 keeps "magulo ang mga magnetic moment sa itaas ng tinatawag na 'freezing temperature'" exactly as the source states it.

Entry 11 is faithful and nothing in it would mislead. Every clause of the Credly notice is kept: the third-party processor authorized by IBM and located in the US, the shared data (pangalan, email address, at badge na nakuha), the uses "pag-uulat ng programa at mga layuning operasyonal", the permissive "Maaaring ibahagi" sharing with subsidiaries and third parties worldwide, and handling "naaayon sa mga kasanayan sa privacy ng IBM". The one thing to fix is that the sentence-final period was moved inside both link texts ("[dito.](...)"), so the period shows up as part of the underlined link. It should be "[dito](...)." as in the English.

examples.source: The IBM Privacy Statement can be viewed [here](https://www.ibm.com/privacy/us/). IBM employees can view the IBM Internal Privacy Statement [here](https://w3.ibm.com/w3publisher/w3-privacy-notice).
examples.translation: Ang IBM Privacy Statement ay maaaring tingnan [dito.](https://www.ibm.com/privacy/us/) Maaaring tingnan ng mga empleyado ng IBM ang IBM Internal Privacy Statement [dito.](https://w3.ibm.com/w3publisher/w3-privacy-notice)
examples.suggested: Maaaring tingnan ang IBM Privacy Statement [dito](https://www.ibm.com/privacy/us/). Maaaring tingnan ng mga empleyado ng IBM ang IBM Internal Privacy Statement [dito](https://w3.ibm.com/w3publisher/w3-privacy-notice).
examples.why: The period sits inside the link text, so it renders as part of the link. This is only cosmetic and the meaning is unchanged. The fronted 'Maaaring tingnan' also reads more naturally than the passive 'ay maaaring tingnan'.

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout and nothing here would mislead a learner. The casual register holds, with no po/opo. The course's core concept, "tools", is rendered two ways: "kasangkapan" in the page description [0] and the English "tool" throughout the overview [4]. In [6], "still under development" became "isinasagawa pa", which means "still being carried out/conducted". A native editor would write "binubuo pa" for a course and exam that are still being built.

examples.source: The exam and badge for this course are still under development.
examples.translation: Ang pagsusulit at badge para sa kursong ito ay isinasagawa pa.
examples.suggested: Ang pagsusulit at badge para sa kursong ito ay binubuo pa.
examples.why: 'isinasagawa' means being carried out/conducted, which suggests the exam is being administered. 'Under development' means it is still being built, so 'binubuo pa' is the right word.

examples.source: Explore modern tools for handling noise and errors
examples.translation: Galugarin ang mga modernong kasangkapan para sa paghawak ng noise at mga error
examples.suggested: Galugarin ang mga modernong tool para sa paghawak ng noise at mga error
examples.why: Entry [4] uses 'tool' for the same concept throughout. Choose one rendering for the course's central term. The page description currently disagrees with the body.

editor_note: Faithful and natural, and every number and condition is kept: "hindi bababa sa 16" of 20 to pass, the lock after "dalawang pagsubok" (it stays "pansamantalang ma-lo-lock"), and the Credly data-sharing notice all match the English, in a casual register with no po/opo.

None of the three rewritten entries would mislead a learner. Entry 3 keeps its meaning, but "pagbubunyag" (revealing) is a loose rendering of "debunking"; "pagpapabulaan" fits better. The two headings are over-translated and no longer match the body. [64] "Pag-aaral ng makina" is a literal calque the field doesn't use, and it can read as "studying machines", while entries 27, 65, 76 and 81 all keep "machine learning". [28] "Simulasyon ng Hamiltonian" is inconsistent with "Hamiltonian simulation" in 27, 35 and 39.

examples.source: Machine learning {#machine-learning}
examples.translation: Pag-aaral ng makina {#machine-learning}
examples.suggested: Machine learning {#machine-learning}
examples.why: Literal calque that Tagalog technical writers don't use, and it can be misread as 'studying machines'. The body text keeps 'machine learning' everywhere (27, 65, 76, 81), so the heading doesn't match the section it introduces.

examples.source: Hamiltonian simulation {#hamiltonian-simulation}
examples.translation: Simulasyon ng Hamiltonian {#hamiltonian-simulation}
examples.suggested: Hamiltonian simulation {#hamiltonian-simulation}
examples.why: It's defensible on its own, but it's inconsistent within the file: entries 27, 35 and 39 all use 'Hamiltonian simulation' as the name of the category.

examples.source: as well as debunking some misconceptions about what it can do
examples.translation: gayundin ang pagbubunyag ng ilang maling akala tungkol sa kung ano ang kaya nitong gawin
examples.suggested: gayundin ang pagpapabulaan sa ilang maling akala tungkol sa kung ano ang kaya nitong gawin
examples.why: 'Pagbubunyag' means revealing or exposing, not refuting. 'Pagpapabulaan' is closer to 'debunking'. The sentence still doesn't mislead.

editor_note: The rewritten heading in entry 32, "3: Operator ng Diffusion", is accurate and would not mislead a learner. It does break consistency with the rest of the page, though. Entry 14 lists the same step as "**Diffusion Operator**", and entries 33 and 35 keep "Diffusion operator" / "diffusion operator". The sibling headings also keep the English term ("1: Initialization", "2: Oracle"). An editor would make the heading "3: Diffusion Operator" so the learner sees the section title match the step it refers to.

examples.source: 3: Diffusion Operator {#3-diffusion-operator}
examples.translation: 3: Operator ng Diffusion {#3-diffusion-operator}
examples.suggested: 3: Diffusion Operator {#3-diffusion-operator}
examples.why: Entries 14, 33 and 35 and the sibling headings 'Initialization' and 'Oracle' all keep the English term. Only this heading uses a different form of the same term, so it does not visibly match list item 3 in entry 14.

editor_note: Entry 26 is faithful and natural: "four qubits precessing at different rates" becomes "apat na qubit na umiikot sa iba't ibang bilis", which matches the page's own use of ikot/rotasyon for Z-axis turns (entries 32 and 34) and of "bilis" for "rates" (entry 44), and it keeps "can be used to encode digits" as "magagamit ... upang mag-encode ng mga digit".

Entry 11 (the Credly notice) keeps every legal point of the English: the US-based processor authorized by IBM, the shared data (pangalan, email address, badge na nakuha), the purposes of use, and global sharing with subsidiaries and third parties. None of that meaning has drifted. The one defect is markup: the sentence-final periods were moved inside the link text as "[dito.](...)", so each link label now ends in a period. The English has "[here](...)." with the period outside. It is cosmetic, but a native editor would put the period back outside the link.

examples.source: The IBM Privacy Statement can be viewed [here](https://www.ibm.com/privacy/us/).
examples.translation: Maaaring tingnan ang IBM Privacy Statement [dito.](https://www.ibm.com/privacy/us/)
examples.suggested: Maaaring tingnan ang IBM Privacy Statement [dito](https://www.ibm.com/privacy/us/).
examples.why: The period was pulled into the link label for both links, so the linked text reads 'dito.'. It belongs outside the link, as in the source.

editor_note: None of the three rewritten entries would mislead a learner. "Plugin ng Rustiq" (23) and "Local mode ng Qiskit AI Transpiler" (33) are faithful and read naturally. The one problem is heading 21, rewritten as "Transpiler na pinapagana ng AI". The rest of the page, including the paragraph right under that heading (22) and entries 7, 61, 85, 87, 98 and 100, uses the name "AI-powered transpiler". So the section heading no longer matches the name the body uses for the method, and it should be aligned with the file's convention.

examples.source: AI-powered transpiler {#ai-powered-transpiler}
examples.translation: Transpiler na pinapagana ng AI {#ai-powered-transpiler}
examples.suggested: AI-powered transpiler {#ai-powered-transpiler}
examples.why: Every other mention on the page (e.g. entry 22 directly below: 'Ang AI-powered transpiler ay gumagamit ng machine learning...') treats 'AI-powered transpiler' as the method's name. Translating only the heading makes the file inconsistent. The meaning is still clear, so this is minor.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout. The caveat that implicit models are cheaper but "mas approximate" than explicit solvent models is kept in [11], and the CASCI comparison and Serverless description in [12]/[14] are accurate. Four things need fixing. Heading [39] was left entirely in English ("Prepare continuum model and mean field object..."). The recommendation line in [48] is ungrammatical ("Kung nakakita ka ng kawili-wili ang gawaing ito"). [18] uses the formal "Mangyaring sumangguni", which clashes with the casual register. Step names are also inconsistent: the headings say "Hakbang 3 at 4" but body entry [43] says "Step 3 (Execute) at Step 4".

examples.source: 1.4: Prepare continuum model and mean field object with relevant variables
examples.translation: 1.4: Prepare continuum model and mean field object with relevant variables
examples.suggested: 1.4: Ihanda ang continuum model at mean field object gamit ang mga kaugnay na variable
examples.why: This heading was not translated at all, while every other step heading was.

examples.source: If you found this work interesting, you might be interested in the following resources:
examples.translation: Kung nakakita ka ng kawili-wili ang gawaing ito, maaaring interesado ka sa mga sumusunod na resources:
examples.suggested: Kung nakita mong kawili-wili ang gawaing ito, baka interesado ka rin sa mga sumusunod na resources:
examples.why: 'nakakita ka ng kawili-wili ang...' is ungrammatical. It mixes two sentence patterns.

examples.source: Please refer to the SQD IEF-PCM Qiskit Function template
examples.translation: Mangyaring sumangguni sa [SQD IEF-PCM Qiskit Function template]
examples.suggested: Tingnan ang [SQD IEF-PCM Qiskit Function template]
examples.why: 'Mangyaring' is formal and does not fit the casual register convention.

examples.source: we combine Step 3 (Execute) and Step 4 (Post-process)
examples.translation: pinagsasama natin ang Step 3 (Execute) at Step 4 (Post-process)
examples.suggested: pinagsasama natin ang Hakbang 3 (Execute) at Hakbang 4 (Post-process)
examples.why: The headings use 'Hakbang' but the body text keeps 'Step', so the two do not match.

editor_note: Entry 105 is faithful: "by" becomes the plural personal marker "nina", which is correct for a list of several authors, and the paper title, author names, affiliation, year and arXiv link are left unchanged, as a citation should be.

The meaning is faithful throughout. The PNA explanation, the parameter caveats (such as "hindi garantisadong monotonic") and the comparison of mitigation strategies all match the English, and nothing would mislead a learner. A few word choices are wrong, though. In [73], "bridges the gap" became "nagbabahagi ng agwat" ("shares the gap"). In [22], inserting correction operations became "pagtutok" ("focusing/aiming"). In [149], "compensates for" became the legalistic "nagbabayad-pinsala", and in [153], "complementary" became "magkakaugnay" ("interrelated"). The terms are also inconsistent: "characterize" appears as kina-characterize, kinakarakter, ikarakter and makakarakter, and the heading in [141] says "Step 4" where every other step heading says "Hakbang".

examples.source: this step bridges the gap between an idealized mirrored circuit and a hardware-ready circuit
examples.translation: ang hakbang na ito ay nagbabahagi ng agwat sa pagitan ng...
examples.suggested: ang hakbang na ito ang tumutulay sa agwat sa pagitan ng...
examples.why: 'nagbabahagi' means 'shares/divides', so the idiom 'bridges the gap' comes out as nonsense.

examples.source: would otherwise come from inserting physical correction operations into the circuit
examples.translation: manggagaling sa pagtutok ng physical correction operations sa circuit
examples.suggested: manggagaling sa pagsisingit ng physical correction operations sa circuit
examples.why: 'pagtutok' means focusing/aiming, not inserting. It also doesn't match 'iturok' in [19].

examples.source: TREX and post-selection offer complementary refinements
examples.translation: nag-aalok ng magkakaugnay na mga pagpapahusay
examples.suggested: nag-aalok ng mga pantulong/karagdagang pagpapahusay na nagpupuno sa isa't isa
examples.why: 'magkakaugnay' means 'interrelated'. That loses the sense of 'complementary' (each adds what the other lacks).

examples.source: effectively compensates for two-qubit gate errors
examples.translation: epektibong nagbabayad-pinsala sa two-qubit gate errors
examples.suggested: epektibong tumutumbas/bumabawi sa two-qubit gate errors
examples.why: 'nagbabayad-pinsala' is the legal sense ('pays damages'). It reads as a calque in a technical context.

examples.source: Step 4: Reconstruct and analyze results
examples.translation: Step 4: I-reconstruct at suriin ang mga resulta
examples.suggested: Hakbang 4: Buuin muli at suriin ang mga resulta
examples.why: Every other step heading, including [44] for the same step, uses 'Hakbang' and 'Buuin muli'.

editor_note: None of the four rewritten entries (8, 21, 34, 50) would mislead a learner. They keep every claim and caveat: the omitted swap network, the reversed bitstring, raw vs. MEM-adjusted counts, and MEM not being able to change feedforward results after the fact. There are three small wording problems. Entry 34 says "implementation" where entry 8 says "implementasyon". Its "hindi kasama ng" reads as "not accompanied by" rather than "omit". Entry 50 renders "parallel" as "kasabay (hiwalay na)", which adds a clumsy gloss in parentheses that the English doesn't have.

examples.source: Both implementations omit the final swap network.
examples.translation: Parehong hindi kasama ng mga implementation ang huling swap network.
examples.suggested: Parehong hindi isinasama ng dalawang implementasyon ang huling swap network.
examples.why: Entry 8 and the rest of the page use 'implementasyon', but this entry leaves it in English. 'hindi kasama ng' is also awkward for 'omit'; 'hindi isinasama' is the natural verb.

examples.source: The parallel `raw_process_fidelity` dictionary retains an unmitigated calculation
examples.translation: Ang kasabay (hiwalay na) `raw_process_fidelity` dictionary ay nagtatabi ng unmitigated na kalkulasyon
examples.suggested: Ang katapat na `raw_process_fidelity` dictionary ay nagtatabi ng unmitigated na kalkulasyon
examples.why: The English has no parenthetical, so the added gloss is clumsy. 'kasabay' suggests something happening at the same time rather than a companion dictionary. A single word such as 'katapat' is cleaner.

examples.source: For fun, make sure to compare these results to your results at the end
examples.translation: Bilang dagdag na kasiyahan, ihambing mo ang mga resultang ito
examples.suggested: Para masaya, ihambing mo ang mga resultang ito sa sarili mong resulta sa dulo
examples.why: 'Bilang dagdag na kasiyahan' is a stiff literal rendering of the casual 'For fun'. It is only a small tone slip, and the meaning is intact.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through. The methodology caveats in [28], [79], [80], [87] and [88] keep their direction: two-qubit errors come out above the reported values, T2 comes out below, and a gap is "hindi awtomatikong ebidensya ng drift". Nothing would mislead a learner. What a native editor would still fix is small. In [85], "noticeably lower" loses its "noticeably". In [57], "this is where you would transpile" becomes a "dapat" (should) instruction. There are a few calques: "Nabubuhay lamang" for "live only" in [27], "pinagtatagni-tagni" for "chains" in [90], and the wrong verb voice in "ang mga eksperimento ay makukuha lamang" in [44]. Some wording also varies within the page: "iniulat" and "naiulat" both appear, "property" and "properties" both appear, and the headings say "Step 1" while the body text says "Hakbang 1".

examples.source: can yield noticeably lower $T_2$ values than the backend reports
examples.translation: ay maaaring magbunga ng mas mababang $T_2$ na halaga kaysa sa iniulat ng backend
examples.suggested: ay maaaring magbunga ng kapansin-pansing mas mababang $T_2$ na halaga kaysa sa iniulat ng backend
examples.why: Drops the qualifier 'noticeably', which weakens the link to the large gap shown in the plot.

examples.source: In most tutorials this is where you would transpile your circuits.
examples.translation: Sa karamihan ng mga tutorial, dito mo dapat i-transpile ang iyong mga circuit.
examples.suggested: Sa karamihan ng mga tutorial, dito karaniwang ini-transpile ang mga circuit.
examples.why: 'dapat' (should) makes a descriptive remark sound like an instruction, but here the utility does the transpiling for you.

examples.source: the experiments would then only recover the numbers you put in yourself
examples.translation: ngunit sa gayon ang mga eksperimento ay makukuha lamang ang mga numerong inilagay mo mismo
examples.suggested: ngunit makakakuha lamang ang mga eksperimento ng mga numerong ikaw mismo ang naglagay
examples.why: Wrong verb focus ('makukuha' is object focus but has an actor subject); the clause reads ungrammatically.

examples.source: The refreshed properties live only in the backend object returned to you.
examples.translation: Nabubuhay lamang ang mga na-refresh na property sa backend object na ibinalik sa iyo.
examples.suggested: Nasa backend object lamang na ibinalik sa iyo ang mga na-refresh na property.
examples.why: Literal calque of 'live'. 'Nabubuhay' means biologically alive.

examples.source: The `run_and_update` method chains everything you did above
examples.translation: Ang `run_and_update` method ay pinagtatagni-tagni ang lahat ng ginawa mo sa itaas
examples.suggested: Pinagsasama-sama ng `run_and_update` method ang lahat ng ginawa mo sa itaas
examples.why: 'pinagtatagni-tagni' suggests patching things together crudely, and the sentence keeps the stiff 'ay' + actor-focus structure.

editor_note: Both rewritten headings are faithful and natural: [34] "I-optimize ang problema para sa pagpapatakbo sa quantum hardware" keeps the "Step N:" form used in [41], and [36] "Gumawa ng mga ISA circuit" matches the ISA circuit wording in [35].

Neither rewritten entry changes the meaning. Entry 79 ("Ang kurso ng IBM Quantum na [Fundamentals of Quantum Algorithms] ni Dr. John Watrous") is faithful and reads naturally. The problem is the course title in entry 9: it is now translated as "Mga Batayan ng Quantum Algorithms", but everywhere else on the page (entries 15, 23 and 79) the same linked course keeps its English title "Fundamentals of quantum algorithms". A learner could take these for two different courses, so pick one form. Keeping the English title in entry 9, to match 15, 23 and 79, is the smallest fix.

examples.source: [Fundamentals of quantum algorithms](/learning/courses/fundamentals-of-quantum-algorithms).
examples.translation: [Mga Batayan ng Quantum Algorithms](/learning/courses/fundamentals-of-quantum-algorithms).
examples.suggested: [Fundamentals of quantum algorithms](/learning/courses/fundamentals-of-quantum-algorithms).
examples.why: The same course is left in English in entries 15, 23 and 79. Translating it only here makes it look like a different course. The translation is also a mixed calque: a Tagalog frame around the English plural "Quantum Algorithms".

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout. The J normalization note, the zero-magnetization argument, the fidelity figures (0.65 and 0.7) and the explanation of why the two-layer fidelity is lower all match the source. The problems are wording and consistency. 'Simulate' is rendered as 'Gayahin' (imitate) in the title and link text [1][86] but 'i-simulate' elsewhere, and 'reproduce' becomes 'ginagaya' [18][83], which softens a replication claim into 'imitate'. AQC appears as 'Tinatayang quantum compiling' in the [37] heading but 'approximate quantum compiling' everywhere else. Several phrasings are stiff or ungrammatical: 'konstrukto' [36], 'ay warm-starts' and perfective 'na-reset' for a recurring action [62], and 'nag-eebolba … ay nagbubunga pagkatapos ng DSF' [35], which can be misread as 'after the DSF'.

examples.source: These observables are constructed once per problem instance
examples.translation: Ang mga observable na ito ay konstrukto nang isang beses lamang
examples.suggested: Binubuo nang isang beses lamang ang mga observable na ito sa bawat problem instance
examples.why: 'konstrukto' is not a Tagalog verb form. The sentence reads as broken MT.

examples.source: A two-dimensional discrete Fourier transform then yields the DSF S(q,ω).
examples.translation: Ang isang two-dimensional discrete Fourier transform ay nagbubunga pagkatapos ng DSF $S(q,\omega)$.
examples.suggested: Pagkatapos, nagbubunga ng DSF na $S(q,\omega)$ ang isang two-dimensional discrete Fourier transform.
examples.why: Putting 'pagkatapos ng' right before 'DSF' reads as 'after the DSF' instead of 'then'. 'nag-eebolba' earlier in the same entry is also awkward.

examples.source: each step warm-starts from the previous step's optimized parameters, and parameters are reset to the stage defaults
examples.translation: ang bawat step ay warm-starts mula sa ... at ang mga parameter ay na-reset sa stage defaults
examples.suggested: nagwa-warm-start ang bawat step mula sa ... at nire-reset ang mga parameter sa stage defaults
examples.why: An English finite verb is dropped into Tagalog syntax, and the perfective 'na-reset' does not fit a process that repeats at every stage boundary.

examples.source: Approximate quantum compiling (AQC)
examples.translation: Tinatayang quantum compiling (AQC)
examples.suggested: Approximate quantum compiling (AQC)
examples.why: Every other entry ([6][11][38][57]) keeps 'approximate quantum compiling'. Only this heading translates it, which splits the term within the file.

examples.source: we reproduce the results of Lee et al.
examples.translation: ginagaya natin ang mga resulta ng
examples.suggested: inuulit/nire-reproduce natin ang mga resulta ng
examples.why: 'ginagaya' means imitate or copy, which is weaker than reproducing published results. The same verb is used for 'Simulate' in the title [1], so two distinct concepts share one word.

editor_note: None of the 17 rewritten entries would mislead a learner. Entry 7 keeps its meaning and hedging ("maaaring sumuporta"), and the step headings (34, 40, 42, 63) match their English. Three small word-choice slips remain. Heading 38 renders "AdaBoost reference" as "sanggunian ng AdaBoost", which sounds like a citation or source, not a comparison baseline (entry 39 uses "reference point"). Heading 72 uses "uso", which in Tagalog leans toward fashion or fad, while the body (71, 73) says "trend". Entry 7 switches to "grid stability" after entry 0 set up "katatagan ng grid".

examples.source: Classical baseline: AdaBoost reference
examples.translation: Classical baseline: sanggunian ng AdaBoost
examples.suggested: Classical baseline: AdaBoost bilang reference
examples.why: 'Sanggunian' usually means a citation or source you look things up in. Here 'reference' means a baseline you compare against, which is how entry 39 uses 'reference point'.

examples.source: Visualize quality trends across configurations
examples.translation: I-visualize ang mga uso sa kalidad sa iba't ibang configuration
examples.suggested: I-visualize ang mga trend sa kalidad sa iba't ibang configuration
examples.why: 'Uso' suggests fashion or fad. The body text right next to it (entries 71, 73) uses 'trend', so the heading doesn't match.

examples.source: Maintaining grid stability is an important challenge...
examples.translation: Ang pagpapanatili ng grid stability ay isang mahalagang hamon...
examples.suggested: Ang pagpapanatili ng katatagan ng grid ay isang mahalagang hamon...
examples.why: Entry 0 introduces 'katatagan ng grid' and entry 6 repeats it, but entry 7 switches to English 'grid stability'. It's a small inconsistency in the opening paragraphs.

editor_note: All four rewritten headings are accurate and use normal Taglish, for example "Transformation ng QUBO" (which matches "mathematical transformation" in [60]) and "Integrated na classical post-processing" (which matches the body wording in [24]). "Iterative optimization ng bias-field" is also defensible.

The meaning holds throughout. The postselection tradeoff, the gamma-score explanation and the hardware shot-budget arithmetic are all faithful, so nothing here would mislead a learner. A native editor would still fix four things. "Committed" is rendered two ways, "kinokomit" [17] and "naisagawa/naisasagawa" [57, 66, 76], and "naisagawa" reads as "performed" rather than "fixed into the circuit". [69] strengthens "most shots" to "halos lahat ng shot" ("almost all"), while [76] correctly uses "karamihan". [14] calques "at the cost of" as "sa gastos ng", and [20] renders "scores a check" as "sumusukat" ("measures"), which doesn't match "nagra-rate/sini-score" used elsewhere.

examples.source: checks are committed sequentially ... a committed check is not changed as more checks are added
examples.translation: naisasagawa ang mga check nang sunud-sunod ... hindi na binabago ang isang naisagawang check
examples.suggested: kinokomit (o 'itinatakda') ang mga check nang sunud-sunod ... hindi na binabago ang isang na-commit na check
examples.why: [17] uses 'kinokomit' for the same concept. 'Naisagawa' means executed/performed, which blurs the idea of a check being fixed into the circuit.

examples.source: At this size, most shots trigger at least one check
examples.translation: Sa laking ito, halos lahat ng shot ay nag-trigger ng kahit isang check
examples.suggested: Sa laking ito, karamihan ng shot ay nagti-trigger ng kahit isang check
examples.why: 'Halos lahat' (almost all) is stronger than 'most'. [76] correctly uses 'karamihan'.

examples.source: at the cost of a reduced postselection rate
examples.translation: sa gastos ng pababang postselection rate
examples.suggested: kapalit ng mas mababang postselection rate
examples.why: 'Sa gastos ng' calques English 'at the cost of'. 'Pababang' (decreasing) is also not quite 'reduced'.

examples.source: selects the function that scores a check
examples.translation: Pinipili ng argument na `cost` ang function na sumusukat ng isang check
examples.suggested: ang function na nagbibigay ng score sa isang check
examples.why: 'Sumusukat' means measures, which is a different operation from scoring. Elsewhere the file uses 'sini-score' and 'nagra-rate'.

editor_note: Entry 33 is faithful: "Abstraktong Circuit, observable" keeps both inputs and pairs cleanly with entry 34's "Target circuit at observable". The capitalized "Circuit" is covered by the separate deterministic sweep, so it is not counted here.
